title: SENT plate at a/W = 0.3 in plane strain: K_I from the J-integral against two handbook fits

gates.quantity: |K_FEM - K_GS| / K_GS at a/W = 0.3, plane strain, finest level
gates.reference: K_I = sigma sqrt(pi a) F(a/W), Tada Paris & Irwin 3rd ed. polynomial fit
gates.note: the tolerance written into the anchor case

gates.quantity: |K_FEM - K_GS| / K_GS at a/W = 0.3, plane strain, finest level

gates.reference: two independent handbook fits for the SENT geometry factor
gates.note: bounds the reference uncertainty; not a numerical result

gates.quantity: max-min of F over 8 fan lines, finest level
gates.reference: J is path independent for a contour enclosing no singularity other than the tip

gates.quantity: |vertical reaction / applied load - 1| at the finest level
gates.reference: global equilibrium of the discrete system

gates.quantity: Roache GCI of F over the three levels
gates.reference: grid convergence index of the finest value from the three values themselves
gates.note: undefined (not converging) is reported as a failed gate, never as a pass

gates.quantity: |F(nu=0.45) - F(nu=0.30)| / F(nu=0.30) at the medium level
gates.reference: LEFM: K_I is independent of E and nu, so a correct E' (and energy density) must cancel nu
gates.note: finest available level is graded; the coarser spread is reported alongside because a wrong E' pair would sit at +4.83 % on every mesh

gates.quantity: |K_(dPi/da) - K_J| / K_J at a/W = 0.3, plane strain
gates.reference: global energy release rate versus the local contour integral on the same field

gates.quantity: |K_(dPi/da) - K_GS| / K_GS at a/W = 0.3, plane strain
gates.reference: K_I = sigma sqrt(pi a) F(a/W), Tada Paris & Irwin 3rd ed.

gates.quantity: max |f.u / U - 2| over the two energy-oracle solves
gates.reference: f.u = 2U for a linear traction-only problem; audits the potential bookkeeping

limitations: linear elastic, small strain, stationary mode-I, homogeneous isotropic material, no body force
plane strain is realised by the constitutive matrix and E' = E/(1-nu^2); no 3-D constraint check is attempted
a/W = 0.3 only: the plane-stress legs at a/W = 0.20/0.35/0.50 live in benchmarks/verified/fem_sent_j_integral
the energy oracle uses a central difference with h = 0.01 W on the same medium discretisation; its O(h^2) truncation error is not separated from discretisation noise
one geometry (H/W = 2) and one load level: height sensitivity is covered by the plane-stress anchor
